claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar five-element alloy.
The WTaTiVZr alloy is homogeneous.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has a predominantly BCC microstructure.
The WTaTiVZr alloy likely has refined grains relative to commercial pure tungsten.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has high lattice distortion.
Increased lattice distortion from multiple refractory elements primarily governs the alloy's high-temperature plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion enhances dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion produces a higher density of active slip systems.
Multi-element alloying activates additional deformation mechanisms such as grain-boundary sliding.
Enhanced dislocation activity produces more uniform and distributed high-temperature plastic deformation.
The proposed deformation mechanism delays crack initiation.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature testing.
WTaTiVZr will absorb more energy before fracture than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will have a lower ductile-to-brittle transition temperature than pure tungsten.
Commercial pure tungsten typically has lower ductility and greater brittleness than WTaTiVZr under the proposed service conditions.
Commercial pure tungsten has a higher ductile-to-brittle transition temperature than WTaTiVZr.
Dislocation-mediated deformation dominates in WTaTiVZr at temperatures of at least 1000 °C.
Irradiation-induced microstructural changes such as bubble formation may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
Processing history, grain size, and secondary phases may affect the quantitative plastic-strain and toughness improvements.
The comparison will apply identical high-temperature mechanical conditions to WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten and monitor plastic strain, toughness, transition temperature, and dislocation behavior.

contradictions.description: The initial-state comparison specifies likely refined WTaTiVZr grains versus coarse-grained tungsten, while the experiment claims controlled microstructures. Unless grain size and other processing variables are explicitly matched, the comparison does not isolate lattice distortion from grain-size effects.
